title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear portions and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, it's essential to provide enough iron and folate to ensure the health of both mother and baby. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports the development of the fetus. In this article, we'll introduce three recipes rich in iron and folate that can be cooked in under 30 minutes, suitable for pregnant women.

## Nutrient Analysis
Iron and folate are two crucial nutrients during pregnancy. Iron helps prevent anemia, while folate supports the development of the nervous system and prevents birth defects. To enhance iron absorption, it's recommended to combine iron-rich foods with vitamin C-rich foods.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken Bowl with Roasted Vegetables
* 100g grilled chicken
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup roasted vegetables (carrots, green beans, bell peppers)
* 1 orange

Grilled chicken is an excellent source of heme iron, while roasted vegetables and orange provide vitamin C. This recipe is simple and easy to cook, perfect for busy pregnant women.

## Recipe 2: Beef and Vegetable Stir-Fry with Egg
* 100g beef stir-fry
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, green beans, bell peppers)
* 1 egg

Beef stir-fry is a good source of heme iron, while mixed vegetables and egg provide vitamin C and folate. This recipe is nutrient-dense and easy to cook.

## Recipe 3: Vegetarian Bowl with Beans and Roasted Vegetables
* 100g cooked beans
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup roasted vegetables (carrots, green beans, bell peppers)
* 1 orange

Cooked beans are a good source of non-heme iron, while roasted vegetables and orange provide vitamin C. This recipe is suitable for pregnant women following a vegetarian diet.

## Food Safety Notes
When cooking for pregnant women, it's essential to prioritize food safety to avoid food poisoning. Choose fresh and clean ingredients, wash them thoroughly, and cook them well. Avoid eating raw or undercooked foods, especially meat, eggs, and seafood.

## Conclusion
The three recipes above provide sufficient iron and folate for pregnant women, while ensuring food safety. Pregnant women can refer to and cook these nutrient-dense and easy-to-make meals. For more information on prenatal nutrition, visit our [meal planner](/planner) or check out [other articles](/blog/topics) on our website.

## When to Seek Help
If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about prenatal nutrition, they should consult their doctor or a registered dietitian. They can provide personalized advice and guidance to ensure the health of both mother and baby.
